findings.reason: naming reset.py:402 as the owner makes three drifting spellings one the reset spec and the backlog sweep share.
findings.text: the section says it removes chunks "through the traversal clear_facility_code uses", but that traversal already exists in two places and the one §27 needs is neither of them: imas_codex/discovery/base/reset.py:402 `_CODE_CHUNK_CASCADE` is exactly this cascade scoped to a node set (rendered at reset.py:419 and :430, the reset-to-discovered/triaged specs that already delete example+chunk nodes), while imas_codex/discovery/code/scanner.py:567-584 spells it a second time inline, facility-wide and by the `facility_id` property. A third spelling, scoped to "status not ingested", drifts from both; §27 is the backlog sweep of the cascade the reset owner already applies per file, so the change is to export/extend `_CODE_CHUNK_CASCADE` in imas_codex/discovery/base/reset.py and apply it scoped, not a third copy

findings.reason: extending relevance_predicate is the difference between one content-gate owner and two that can diverge.
findings.text: the content-ingest gate already has one owner, `relevance_predicate` at imas_codex/discovery/code/scorer.py:91 (which already parameterises the stage and the threshold), and it is what every gate site renders today: the ingest claim imas_codex/discovery/code/workers.py:707, the pending-ingest count imas_codex/discovery/code/parallel.py:455, the pending-chunk-embed count imas_codex/discovery/code/parallel.py:503, and the has-work check imas_codex/discovery/code/graph_ops.py:747. The plan's own four gate sites are exactly those four, so the honest change is to add an optional facet clause to `relevance_predicate` so that all four keep one owner; the section's "one owner, beside relevance_predicate" places a second predicate beside it and leaves a future content-gate site that calls `relevance_predicate` silently facet-blind. The four facet names are likewise already owned by `SCORE_DIMENSION_NAMES` (scorer.py:44) and `FACET_QUESTION_FIELDS` (scorer.py:113) — they must be read from those, not hand-spelled

findings.reason: the section should extend the existing Python relevance function rather than add a parallel mirror of the same rule.
findings.text: the plan's "one Python function mirrors it" reproduces an admission check that already exists in Python: `scope_relevance`/`triage_relevance` (imas_codex/discovery/code/scorer.py:223 and :228) are the Python owner of "largest of the four scope nouls", and the admission is already computed in Python at imas_codex/discovery/code/parallel.py and imas_codex/discovery/code/workers.py:578 (`triage_relevance(...) >= ingest_threshold`). A fresh mirror that re-states the facet list and the OR-of-facets rule alongside the Cypher predicate is two owners of one rule; the mirror should be the facet-augmented form of the existing Python relevance function, sharing `SCORE_DIMENSION_NAMES`, so the Cypher and Python arms cannot drift

findings.reason: the reset spec as it stands leaves 17 skipped files unrejudged and forces a name-arm re-enrich pass the plan does not budget.
findings.text: the section resets the 235 not-ingested files "to triaged through reset_to_status with a status filter", but the cited mechanism does not match that use. `reset_to_status` (imas_codex/discovery/base/reset.py:66) takes `extra_filter` (a Cypher fragment starting with `AND`), not a status filter, and the `CodeFile` `triaged` spec (reset.py:426) has `source_statuses=["scored","ingested","enriched"]` — it excludes `skipped`, so the 17 skipped files in the 235 the section names are not covered by that spec; and it clears `_CODE_ENRICH_FIELDS` (reset.py:363, including `is_enriched`), while the score stage's pending predicate requires `status='triaged'` AND `is_enriched = true` (imas_codex/discovery/code/parallel.py:445-447), so a plain reset-to-triaged drops the enrichment the content arm reads and forces a full name-arm re-enrichment the section does not mention. The node must either pass an `extra_filter` covering `skipped` and account for the re-enrich pass, or use a reset spec shaped for a content-only re-judge

rubric_items.deep_module: pass — §27 hides the cascade, the live-claim exclusion and the embed window behind one operational node, and §26 hides the facet rule behind one predicate rendered at every gate site; neither spreads its logic over many small wrappers.
rubric_items.duplicate_owner: a finding — §27 re-spells the CodeExample/CodeChunk cascade that already exists twice, and §26 splits the content-ingest gate away from relevance_predicate, its current owner.
rubric_items.interface_budget: pass — the supplied counts are public_definitions 0, cli_options 0, mcp_views 0, refusal_families 0; §26 adds only a [tool.imas-codex.discovery] threshold beside the two existing thresholds and an accessor in settings.py, §27 adds no interface at all, so neither section opens a new family to account for.
rubric_items.reuse_search: pass — §26 names scorer.relevance_predicate and the settings threshold owner (imas_codex/settings.py get_code_...), and §27 names the clear_facility_code chunk traversal, so both searched before proposing; two specifics are wrong and are raised below.
rubric_items.thin_wrapper: a finding — §26 adds a second admission predicate beside relevance_predicate rather than extending the owner the gate already renders at all four ingest sites.
